newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock indices end down on clampdown fears.
newsitem.headline: China stock indices end down on clampdown fears.

text.p: China stocks ended sharply lower on Tuesday as talk of new government measures to cool down trading swirled through the markets, brokers said.

The Shanghai B index fell 2.479 points, or 2.59 percent, to 93.315 points, off an intraday low of 92.061 points on some institutional support just before the close. The Shenzhen B index plunged 5.13 points, or 2.80 percent, to 178.37.
Brokers said some rumours referred to the possibility of the government allowing some previously non-tradeable institutional shares to enter the secondary market.
"This could hugely inflate the market size and the existing funds may not be able to provide sufficient support," an analyst said.
Securities authorities were also said to be planning to extend the transaction settlement period to three days to reduce market volatility, brokers said.
This compares with the current settlement period of one day for A shares and immediate settlement for B shares.
"This could dry up market liquidity," a J&A analyst said.
A Hong Kong newspaper on Tuesday said Chinese authorities had decided they would no longer tolerate the recent "crazy" market gains, and would announce clampdown measures in the short term.
"Apart from extending the settlement period, the government is also seen likely to rein in several brokerages," an analyst at a major investment bank said.
On the Shanghai B share market, Shanghai Vacuum & Electron Device was the biggest loser on institutional unwinding selling, plunging $0.024, or 9.83 percent, to $0.220 on volume of 967,100 shares.
Shanghai Worldbest was the most actively traded, supported by one major institution late in the session despite heavy unwinding selling, ending unchanged at $0.740 on volume of 3.6 million shares.
Chiwan Wharf Holdings Ltd was the worst performer on the Shenzhen B share market, losing HK$0.38, or 6.69 percent, to HK$5.30.
The indices are seen as having the potential to move sharply in either direction in the short term, given the market's volatile mood, analysts said.
"It's very hard to make a bet now," an analyst at J&A Securities said. "People are poking their ears up to try to sense what the government may do."
Shanghai's A index closed sharply down for the same reason, with heavy profit-taking depressing the market, brokers said.
The index fell 37.693 points, or 2.40 percent, to 1,531.306 on volume of 946.8 million shares worth 12.9 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index dipped 103.034 points, or 2.40 percent, to 4,183.148 points.
The Shenzhen A share index ended 14.50 points, or 2.65 percent, lower at 531.52 on turnover of 16.3 billion yuan.
